title: Telangana Woman Killed in Missouri Truck Crash; Family Seeks Help to Bring Body Home
excerpt: Daram Supriya, 31, from Mahabubabad district, died after a speeding truck hit her car in Missouri; the family has appealed for help bringing her body home for final rites.
body:
• Daram Supriya, 31, from Maripeda in Telangana's Mahabubabad district, died after the car she was traveling in was hit from behind by a speeding truck in Missouri on Saturday evening (October 4, around 2:00 a.m. IST).
  • Supriya died on the spot; another Indian woman in the same car sustained serious injuries and was rushed to a nearby hospital. Local police have begun investigating the exact cause.
  • The family, in deep shock, has appealed to the government and officials for help bringing her body back to India quickly for final rites.
  • She was married and is survived by her husband Kodumuri Ranjith and her in-laws in Mahabubabad town.

A 31-year-old woman from Telangana was killed in a road crash in Missouri, USA, after the car she was traveling in was rammed from behind by a speeding truck. Daram Supriya, a native of Maripeda in Mahabubabad district, died on the spot on Saturday evening local time — around 2:00 a.m. IST on Sunday, October 4.

The crash

"She was married and is survived by her husband Kodumuri Ranjith and her in-laws in Mahabubabad town."

According to Telugu media reports, Supriya was living and working in Missouri in connection with her employment. The car she was in was struck from behind by a truck traveling at speed. Another Indian woman who was in the same car suffered serious injuries and was taken to a nearby hospital; her identity and condition were not reported. Local police have started an investigation into the exact cause of the accident. The IndiaToday slug for the story references a St. Louis-area crash, though the specific highway or town within Missouri has not been confirmed by the Telugu press.

A family in shock, appealing for help

News of Supriya's death plunged her family into deep shock, according to press reports. She is survived by her husband, Kodumuri Ranjith, and her in-laws Kodumuri Venkateshwarlu and Radhika, who live at Veerabhadra Apartments in Mahabubabad town. The family has requested the government and officials for help in bringing her body back to India quickly so that final rites can be performed. As of publication, no fundraiser had been reported, and no government official's intervention had been named.

Diaspora angle

This is the latest in a recurring string of tragedies involving Telugu workers and students in the United States, where families back home must navigate the slow, expensive process of repatriating a loved one's remains. In similar cases, families typically coordinate with the Indian consulate for the required clearances and documentation before the body can be flown home — a process that can take several days. For the Mahabubabad family, speed now matters: their only ask is help getting Supriya home for her final rites.

What's next

Local police are investigating the crash, and the family awaits updates. Community groups in the US Telugu diaspora have frequently stepped in during such crises — pooling funds for repatriation when families cannot afford it — though no organized effort had surfaced for this case at the time of publication.
